prose: The Mac App Store is hosting lookalike rip-offs trading on Muse, Instagram, and VLC, and the receipts are user reviews from people who paid before realizing their mistake. One reviewer 'subscribed because I confused this service with Meta Muse'; others describe an Instagram-lookalike that seizes the screen with an unclosable free-trial popover that converts to a paid subscription and even ignores 'Quit App', forcing users to force-quit or delete the app to regain control. The post compares the two Muse listings side by side: Meta's is subtitled 'Your personal AI agent' while the copycat runs 'Your professional AI Agent', with near-identical screenshot headers ('Approve what gets sent or spent' vs 'Approve what gets sent or connect') and an opening description copied almost word for word.
highlights: Mac App Store listings are imitating Muse, Instagram, and VLC, per user reviews and listing comparisons
One user subscribed after confusing the copycat with Meta Muse, then asked for a refund
The Instagram lookalike locks the screen behind an unclosable free-trial popover and ignores Quit
Copycat Muse subtitles itself 'Your professional AI Agent' against Meta's 'Your personal AI agent'
Screenshot headers and the app description are copied nearly word for word
Users report having to force-quit or delete the app to escape the paywall
